thread:
Incident Bot: PAGING: multiple customer reports — console shows route config A but API returns route B for paging endpoints. Partial UI failure and failed handshakes. Paging severity: P1. Paging alerts triggered at 18:09 UTC.
Elena (SRE): I'm on the bridge. Observed spike in 502s from console → control-plane API. Confirming whether control plane propagated the latest paging toggle.
Ryan (Eng): pulling logs now, tagging. Might be a propagation race between rollout service and the control-plane cache invalidator.
Maya (Support): I've received three customer escalations (acct: neatlytics, corp-zen) — they see different paging behavior in console vs API. They're blocking.
Jordan (Ops): oncall rotation switched 18:15 UTC — handing over to Elena. I'm standing by for mitigation steps.
Elena (SRE): Quick assessment — console is reading config from cache layer X (regional cache), control-plane API reads from authoritative store. Cache mismatch looks likely. Can we force a cache invalidate for the region?
Ryan (Eng): prepping a safe cache flush. Proposed mitigation: 1) toggle read-through to authoritative store for 10s; 2) invalidate local cache shards; 3) fallback route to stable paging v1 if propagation fails.
Sam (Product): Customer impact: UI shows wrong 'paged' toggles which can double-request users. Priority high for accounts on dedicated capacity.
Audrey (DevEx): Adding note: telemetry shows increased duplicate token billing for a small subset. Need to track for billing reconcile.
Elena (SRE): Action list: @Ryan do cache invalidate and feature-flag rollback if needed. @Jordan prepare POST-incident communication template. @Maya compile affected customer list. I'll watch metrics and confirm rollback if errors go down.
Ryan (Eng): Running invalidation in staging first. Command I'll run (prod after stage):
```
# invalidate region-secondary-cache
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal/invalidates/cache" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","shard":"paging-*"}'
```
Ryan (Eng): staging invalidate returned 200 and console config reflects authoritative store. Moving to prod in 2 mins.
Jordan (Ops): Ready for prod window. I have escalation path to 2nd line infra if flush blocks.
Maya (Support): Noted — telling customers we're investigating with ETA ~15m.
Elena (SRE): Executed prod invalidation at 18:22 UTC. Watching error rates.
Ryan (Eng): Prod invalidation returned 200. Logs below from sync worker:
```
[18:22:15] sync-worker.INFO - shard paging-03 invalidated
[18:22:16] sync-worker.INFO - propagation job queued to control-plane-cache-refresher
[18:22:18] refresher.INFO - updated cache key paging-config:SUCCESS
```
Elena (SRE): Metrics: UI 502s fell from 9% -> 1.2% over 120s, paging handshake lat p99 down from 2.8s -> 0.9s. Partial recovery visible.
Maya (Support): Customers report console is behaving better. Two accounts confirm resolved. One account still sees mismatch (corp-zen).
Ryan (Eng): Checking corp-zen tenant logs — control-plane show a stale config read at 18:21:50, but cache refresh for their shard skipped due to rate-limiter. Found this in refresher logs:
```
[18:21:51] refresher.WARN - rate-limited key=paging-config:corp-zen
[18:21:51] refresher.DEBUG - limiter tokens=0/5
```
Ryan (Eng): Hypothesis: rate-limiter allowed partial propagation; backoff prevented immediate fallback for that tenant.
Elena (SRE): Mitigation 2: disable rate-limiter for refresher for 2 minutes for affected shards. Ryan can you do a targeted override?
Ryan (Eng): Doing targeted override for corp-zen now. Command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal/refresh/override" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"corp-zen","mode":"force"}'
```
Ryan (Eng): override accepted 18:26:04. refresher logs: 
```
[18:26:05] refresher.INFO - forced refresh tenant=corp-zen status=OK
[18:26:06] refresher.INFO - cache updated paging-config:corp-zen
```
Elena (SRE): corp-zen reports good after 18:27 UTC. All known customers reporting recovery.
Sam (Product): Good. Please capture timeline and root cause signals for RCA. Key ask: did control-plane store have correct config at initial write or was an earlier write incorrect?
Ryan (Eng): I'm checking controller write history. Found a write at 18:19:10 with config V2 for paging; write succeeded and was persisted. The issue was propagation to cache layer; no evidence of an incorrect authoritative write.
Elena (SRE): So root cause hypothesis: propagation backlog + rate-limiter on refresher caused partial cache staleness -> console read stale config -> UI/API mismatch.
Audrey (DevEx): Any downstream mitigations to avoid user duplicate requests? We should consider short-term UI-side debouncing while propagation guarantees are being strengthened.
Jordan (Ops): Ops follow-up: I'm opening a runbook task to add telemetry on refresh-limiter drops and an emergency bypass button for SRE.
Maya (Support): I'll send confirmed customer list and draft language. Will mark accounts for billing reconciliation if duplicates occurred.
Elena (SRE): For RCA thread: we need timeline (I'll paste), logs (Ryan you have refresher logs), mitigation steps, and action items (cache invalidation automation, limiter tuning, emergency bypass).
Ryan (Eng): Pasting condensed timeline to include in RCA:
```
18:09:00 - alerts triggered (incidents funnel)
18:15:10 - initial paging toggle write (V2) persisted to control-plane
18:19:10 - refresher job queued for full propagation
18:21:50 - refresher rate-limited for some shards
18:22:15 - SRE initiated cache invalidation
18:26:04 - forced override for tenant corp-zen
18:27:00 - customers report recovery
```
Sam (Product): Also include potential impact on billing and recommend offering credits for affected customers.
Elena (SRE): Agreed. I'm flagging action owners: Ryan - implement targeted bypass + alert when limiter blocks > threshold; Jordan - runbook and emergency bypass UI; Audrey - UX debounce proposal; Maya - customer comms + ledger list for billing ops.
Ryan (Eng): I'll open the engineering ticket and attach the refresher logs and traces. Ticket will include proposed change: exponential refill + burst allowance for critical tenant flows.
Jordan (Ops): I'll coordinate with infra to add a temporary SRE bypass (requires HSM token approval). ETA 3 days for secure bypass; short-term we'll document manual override steps.
Maya (Support): customers updated and follow-ups scheduled. No further escalations at the moment.
Incident Bot: Incident transitioned to MITIGATED at 18:33 UTC. Please continue with RCA in this thread and tag #postmortems when ready. :white_check_mark:
Elena (SRE): Closing on-call handoff notes: handoff to postmortem lead Audrey. Saving logs to /incidents/1830126789/artifacts.
Audrey (DevEx): I'll draft the RCA and include timeline, logs, and the proposed changes. Will ping product/finance about credits.
Ryan (Eng): Any other observations? I noticed the control-plane->cache propagator uses a single queue per region; we should consider sharding by tenant groups to avoid hotness. Adding to ticket.
Sam (Product): Thanks everyone. Great coordination.
Maya (Support): tagging customers done. Will help with postmortem comms.
Elena (SRE): Thanks team. Leaving follow-ups in the ticket.
Audrey (DevEx): I'll aim to post a first-draft RCA in ~24h.
